---
th Order No. 15/ Dated: 4 November, 2025 I.A. No. 11985 of 2025 Heard Mr. Rana Surjit Singh,
learned counsel appearing for the appellant, learned A.P.P. assisted by Dr. Suvendu Jaipuriar,
learned counsel appearing for the informant.
2. This interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.
3. The prayer for bail of the appellant was earlier dismissed as not pressed.

4. The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable u/s- 376 (D) of the I.P.C. and Section 6 of POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years along with a fine of Rs.
10,000/-.
5. Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that it could not be ascertained that the appellant was also involved in committing rape upon the victim.
6. It has been submitted that the appellant is in custody since long.
7. Learned A.P.P. as well as the learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
8. It appears that while the victim was sleeping in her house, the appellant and two other accused persons had taken her to a lonely place where she was subjected to rape.

Although it appears that the incident had taken place on 22.09.2019, the First Information Report was instituted on 24.09.2019, consequent to which the victim was examined on 25.09.2019, but several injuries were Vicky Oraon vs The State Of Jharkhand on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192169291/
1 found on her person, which has led to an opinion of the concerned doctor that sexual assault could not be ruled out.

sentences.text: The victim has been examined as P.W-4 and she has categorically stated about the appellant and the other accused persons involved in committing rape upon her.
9. Regard being had to the aforesaid facts, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail.
His prayer for bail is hereby rejected.
